column2: All Israel's congregation assembles as one man from Dan through Beersheba with Gilead before the Lord at Mizpah; the eastern land is not omitted.
All tribes stand in God's people's assembly, four hundred thousand sword-bearing infantry; division retains the unusual collective klima.
column3: Division's exact institutional sense requires lexical review; no chiefs or cornerstones are substituted from another tradition.

column2: Benjamin hears of Israel's ascent before the Lord at Mizpah; the assembly asks where, not how, this wickedness occurred.
The narrator calls the woman murdered before the Levite begins his account of coming to Gibeah with his concubine to lodge.
The Levite claims the men intended to kill him and says they violated and mocked his concubine and she died; this remains his speech.
column3: His account does not mention his own handing her over in 19:25; the translator must not add that omission back into his speech or rewrite the narrator to match it.

column2: He admits seizing, dismembering and distributing her throughout Israel's inherited territory, explaining his action by their folly; the assigned agency remains.
Behold, all Israel's sons, word and counsel remain the closing appeal to the assembly.
column3: Give your word and counsel compresses the Greek reflexive give-to-yourselves formulation; deliberation among the assembled Israelites is intended, not a private promise to the speaker.

column2: The assembly rises as one man and collectively refuses both dwelling and house; the parallel negative clauses remain.
Their proposed action against Gibeah is by lot, continuing into the supply arrangement; no missing battle plan is supplied.
Ten per hundred, one hundred per thousand and one thousand per ten thousand consistently set aside a tenth for provisions; the response to all Gibeah's folly remains their announced purpose.
The men gather from their cities as one man, retaining the collective image already used in verses 1 and 8.
The tribes send throughout Benjamin and ask about the wickedness among them; the accusation begins before the demand for specific men.
The demand names impious men, sons of Belial, for execution and removal of wickedness; Benjamin refuses to listen to their Israelite brothers.
Benjamin gathers from its cities to Gibeah to fight Israel; no peace negotiations are added after the refusal.
The selected muster is twenty-five thousand from the cities plus seven hundred chosen young Gibeah men; the sentence continues into their skill description.
Skilled with both hands preserves amphoterodexioi, not left-handed only; all these slingers aim at a hair without missing.
Israel's separate four-hundred-thousand muster excludes Benjamin and identifies all as sword-bearing warriors; the total repeats verse 2.
The inquiry is at Bethel and asks who should lead; the Lord names Judah, without an added assurance of first-day victory.
Israel rises and camps against Gibeah; the short preparatory notice remains separate from the battle formation.
All Israel's men go out and draw up for battle against Benjamin at Gibeah; repeated battle wording is retained.
Benjamin emerges from the city and strikes twenty-two thousand Israelites down to the ground that day; the first defeat's count remains.
Israel strengthens itself and again forms for battle in the first day's place; again reflects the explicit renewed-action construction.
Weeping lasts until evening; the plural people speak with a collective singular I and my brother, while the Lord's go-up command is plural.
The approach is explicitly on the second day, preserving the sequence after the renewed inquiry.
The second day is repeated, with eighteen thousand Israelite sword-bearers struck to the ground by Benjamin from Gibeah.
All Israel and all the people go to Bethel, weep, fast that day and offer whole burnt offerings of deliverance; the selected genitive construction remains.
column3: The Greek has holokautomata soteriou, without an and introducing a second offering type; no harmonization to burnt offerings and peace offerings is made. The ritual expression remains provisional.

column2: The inquiry is followed by the ark's presence there in those days, continuing into Phinehas's service in verse 28.
Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron stands before the ark; the singular inquiry asks whether to fight again or cease, and the Lord promises tomorrow's delivery.
column3: Go up is plural but your hand is singular, with him referring collectively to Benjamin; ordinary English does not expose every number change, which is recorded here.

column2: Israel places ambushes all around Gibeah; the plural ambush noun is retained.
The third-day formation repeats the previous occasions; once and once is rendered idiomatically in its repeated-battle context.
Benjamin is drawn out and strikes about thirty on the two roads, one to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field; all location details remain.
Benjamin interprets the retreat as another defeat, while Israel intends flight to lure them onto the roads; both speeches remain distinct.
Israel forms at Baal-tamar while the ambush struggles from west of Gibeah; the selected western direction is retained.
column3: Struggled forward interprets epalaien with its from-place phrase as advancing struggle; wrestled is the closer lexical image and remains a review question.

column2: Ten thousand selected Israelites arrive opposite Gibeah and battle intensifies; the they unaware of disaster is left as the selected pronoun.
column3: Benjamin is the contextual referent of they despite the immediately preceding Israelite subject; no Greek explicit renaming is claimed.

column2: The Lord routes Benjamin, and Israel strikes twenty-five thousand one hundred sword-bearers that day; the precise count is not rounded to match verse 46.
Benjamin sees its rout; Israel's prior yielding is explained by trust in the ambush, with English had marking the narrative return to the tactic.
The ambush rushes and pours toward Gibeah, then strikes the whole city by the sword; collective and plural actions remain in natural English.
The agreed city-smoke signal links the main force and ambush; signal renders the beacon function of pyrsos in this smoky context.

Propose strike down about thirty men of Israel instead of the added killing clause: typtein traumatias is represented as a combined casualty-producing predicate without separately declaring every casualty dead.
column3: Traumatias can denote wounded casualties, with fatality requiring context; the retained strike down allows that uncertainty. Surely renders plen's emphatic force in Benjamin's boast, not an exclusive only.

column2: The signal rises as a smoke pillar, Benjamin looks back and look marks the city's destruction rising to heaven; the destruction image is retained.
Israel turns back while Benjamin hurries and realizes disaster has reached it; no added fear verb replaces the selected haste.
Flight toward the wilderness is overtaken by battle, and those from the cities destroy them in their midst; the ambiguous group reference remains.
column3: Which cities and which immediate group their midst identifies require narrative assessment; neither is supplied as a new explicit source detail.

column2: The selected cutting down, putting to rest and trampling extend eastward opposite Gibeah; the disturbing rest image remains.
column3: To put them to rest represents katapausai auton katapausin; its precise force as cessation or death-language requires review rather than a substituted pursuit formula.

column2: Eighteen thousand Benjaminites fall, followed by with-all-these mighty men; the unusual prepositional description is retained.
column3: With all these is not silently replaced by all of them; the relation of the mighty men phrase to the count remains syntactically open.

column2: Flight to Rimmon is followed by gleaning five thousand along the roads and two thousand struck as far as Gadaam; the gleaning metaphor remains.
column3: The Israelites is an English supplied subject for the pursuing group inferred from the battle, while the Greek shifts subjects without naming them here.

column2: The selected total is twenty-five thousand sword-bearers, with the repeated mighty-men expression; it differs by one hundred from verse 35 and is retained.
column3: Eighteen thousand plus five thousand plus two thousand equals twenty-five thousand; the earlier muster of twenty-five thousand plus seven hundred equals twenty-five thousand one hundred plus six hundred survivors. These observations record the figures, not a harmonizing correction.

column2: Six hundred reach Rimmon and stay four months; both survival count and duration remain.
Israel hems in Benjamin and strikes city after city, including livestock and everything found, then burns the cities; the scope of violence is not narrowed to soldiers.
